subject: Midcycle invoice spike — fallthrough reroute caused embed counts
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia@brightline.co>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@procura.com>
Date: 2028-04-15T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden midcycle spike — embed charges tripled

Hi Vanessa,

We noticed a sharp jump on our midcycle invoice for Brightline — embed units are ~3x what we saw last week despite no intentional change on our side. We migrated a small subset of traffic to your new streaming endpoint last Tuesday (config id: brt-stream-03) and expected lower token counts, not higher.

I attached our usage export for the last 7 days (brightline_usage_export_20280414.csv). Can your team confirm why embed units were billed instead of streaming tokens? We're seeing many lines labeled as "embed" in the billing export while our app only calls the streaming route.

This is blocking our finance team — can you triage and let us know whether this is billable or if an adjustment is required?

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Integrations
Brightline Retail

Attachment: brightline_usage_export_20280414.csv (csv, 124KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@brightline.co>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-04-15T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden midcycle spike — embed charges tripled

Hi Alicia — thanks for the quick note and the export. Sorry for the disruption; I understand the urgency. I've looped in Karthik (billing) and Marissa (support) to pull logs and start a reconciliation.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm the public app key or customer_id used for the streaming calls (your export shows multiple keys).
- Did you toggle any routing flags like "reroute_on_error" or a custom fallback in the past 10 days?

Karthik / Marissa — can you take a first pass on whether the spike is coming from a routing fallback or a duplicate attribution? If we see a fallthrough to an embedding service, we'll need the prefix match logs (I requested redwood_prefix_match_log_20280415.txt from infra).

I'll update Alicia within 48 hours with a plan.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Lead, Americas
Redwood Inference

> 
> We noticed a sharp jump on our midcycle invoice for Brightline — embed units are ~3x what we saw last week despite no intentional change on our side...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-04-16T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden midcycle spike — embed charges tripled (investigation notes)

Vanessa / Marissa — pulled the routing and prefix logs for Brightline (customer_id: BR-9342) for 2028-04-12 to 2028-04-15. Quick summary:

- Between 2028-04-13T03:10 and 2028-04-14T07:40 UTC we observed ~12k requests that were expected to go to the streaming model (route: brt-stream-03) but returned transient 503s from the primary pool.
- The customer has a fallthrough policy configured (policy id: pb-fall-01) which routes failures to a compatible model. In this case the policy accidentally matched a reranker/embedding variant due to a header mismatch (accept: application/vnd.redwood.embed+json).
- The reroute caused our metering pipeline to tag these requests as "embed" units. Because the embed meter counts per input-item rather than per-token in that execution path, the same payload was billed as N embed units (one per item) instead of M streaming tokens — hence the apparent spike.

Attached I included a short extract of the prefix match log and the routing decision timeline for the window (redwood_prefix_match_log_20280415.txt). Notes: we can see the header mismatch on lines 4127-4133 where the routing rule evaluated to the embed variant.

Recommendations / next steps:
1) Apply a rule patch to fallthrough matching to ensure streaming requests that fail remain classified under streaming-metering when payloads match streaming schema (in progress, rollout ETA 2028-04-19).
2) Pro-rate a credit for the misbilled embed units between 2028-04-13 and 2028-04-14 for account BR-9342. I computed an initial credit estimate of 24,320 embed units (approx $1,214) — that's a starting point, will refine with exact per-unit rate from finance.
3) Offer a temporary protective rule that prevents fallthrough to embedding variants for accounts with active streaming routes (we can enable per-account config).

Files attached for reconciliation: redwood_prefix_match_log_20280415.txt (snippet), routing_decision_20280413-0415.log (internal).

Karthik Iyer
Billing Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_prefix_match_log_20280415.txt (txt, 8KB)
Attachment: routing_decision_20280413-0415.log (log, 96KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia@brightline.co>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@procura.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-04-18T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden midcycle spike — embed charges tripled (resolution & credit)

Hi Alicia / Tom — thanks for your patience while we investigated. Short version: we found an unintended fallthrough to an embedding variant for a subset of streaming requests during 2028-04-13 to 2028-04-14 caused by a routing header mismatch. That resulted in those calls being counted under the embed meter rather than the streaming meter.

What we're doing now:
- We will issue a pro-rated billing credit for Brightline of 24,320 embed units (estimated value: $1,214). Finance will post this as a negative line on your May statement; I'll confirm the exact dollar figure once finance finalizes the per-unit pricing.
- Engineering will ship a fix to fallthrough matching rules on 2028-04-19 to prevent this class of misclassification.
- As a safeguard we've enabled an account-level protection for BR-9342 that prevents fallback to embedding variants while a streaming route is active.

Requested from you: please confirm the app key you want us to apply the temporary protection to (reply with the key id). Once you confirm we'll ensure the protection is immediate.

Apologies for the impact — we know unexpected invoice deltas are painful. We're committed to making this right and improving our routing guardrails so it doesn't recur.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Account Lead, Americas
Redwood Inference
